newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond yield curve steepens.

text.p: *Australian bonds ended showed modest gains after a lighter than of late trading session with the short-end supported by the possibility of a further domestic rate cut before year-end.
*Another dual currency samurai bond issue aided the tone.

Australian bonds showed modest gains after a lighter than of late trading session with the short-end remaining supported by the possibility of a further domestic rate cut before year-end, traders said.

This caused the yield curve to steepen and a further tightening in spread against the U.S., although the long-end continues to find resistance in compressing below 110 basis on the 10-year margin. "The tone is still firm and the offshore still seems to like us, but the turnover has been far from great," one trader said.
A 20 billion three-year dual currency samurai bond issue by New South Wales Treasury Corp also aided the firmer tone.
Although local fundamentals remain constructive, the market remains overshadowed by developments in the U.S. ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Econonmists at Westpac have factored in post-U.S. election rate rises which will cause some tumult in financial markets.

"(But) in the short term at least stronger domestic inflation and fiscal fundamentals and the domestic bias towards easing will allow domestic bonds to ride this coming storm out relatively well," they said in a report.

Local bonds also outperformed Canadian debt where supply pressures weighed on the market after its 10-year bond auction. The New Zealand market continued to benefit from a strong N.Z. dollar, reclaiming some of its recent lost ground against other dollar bonds.
